task: Evolve Creator Launch OS into the free premium flagship for the Starlight template portfolio.
surface: Editorial storefront, signature release-console hero, one operating narrative, catalog, and open-source contract
audience: Independent creators, authors, educators, small studios, template buyers, and implementation clients
first_read: Your work can feel singular, remain yours, and still be simple to buy.
standards: GSAP core, timeline, ScrollTrigger, and performance skills

references.label: Creator Launch OS product contract
references.reason: Protects the honest zero-secret storefront, demo checkout, and activation contract.

references.label: Premium page specification
references.reason: Defines the static composition, product truth, responsive routes, and release gates.

references.label: GSAP scene brief
references.reason: Limits motion to one signature hero, one operating narrative, bounded pointer depth, and complete cleanup.

keep: Editorial publishing character and warm paper system
Real release-console proof and honest demo labels
Server-first routes, accessible states, and zero-secret deployment
avoid: Generic glass-card grids, orbit or node diagrams, and decorative bubble fields
Fake revenue, testimonials, customers, checkout, analytics, or delivery claims
Motion-dependent meaning, custom cursor replacement, and pinned mobile layouts
Uninspected generated media and configuration that suppresses build errors
direction.signature: A real release console resolves through proof, delivery, and ownership lenses inside an editorial kinetic-publishing stage.
system: Tier C exact product interface as the primary proof asset
Dark mineral hero with warm paper narrative and restrained coral, acid, and blue roles
One GSAP hero timeline and one earned ScrollTrigger narrative
Static, mobile, coarse-pointer, JavaScript-free, and reduced-motion routes
Optional Tier B video only after owned export inspection

asset_quality.why_premium: The actual release console proves the product mechanism; liquid lenses are meaningful signal frames rather than substitute artwork.

artifacts.notes: Defines desktop, mobile, pointer, reduced-motion, cleanup, and media behavior.

Inspected at 1440x1000 and 390x844 in the production build. The release console, semantic lenses, mobile narrative fallback, catalog, and declared-background contrast all preserve hierarchy without horizontal overflow.

Inspected in the production build: all three scrubbed ScrollTrigger beats transition correctly; reduced motion clears GSAP transforms and the CSS signal animation; coarse pointers retain the static proof route.

Vercel deployment dpl_vfdhhbQntmK49yZPaTSas4SCVY2g is READY on commit c6e9e13884b0c93de1a4ed11d3e0c84df9094ce3. HTTP, headers, route smoke, and runtime logs were inspected; the same production artifact was visually inspected locally because the team preview is SSO protected.
The mobile header fits at 390px without overflow and now preserves a 44px minimum interaction target for each primary navigation link.

checks.name: asset-tier
checks.evidence: Tier C exact release-console interface selected as the primary artifact; decorative media is explicitly subordinate.

checks.name: product-boundary
checks.evidence: The zero-secret, demo checkout, sample-data, and delivery activation contract is preserved.

checks.name: implementation
checks.evidence: Premium source composition and GSAP boundary are implemented; 14/14 contract tests and the Anti-Slop verifier at 100/100 pass.

checks.name: contrast-guardrail
checks.evidence: Small muted labels were raised above the declared ink/paper contrast floors, and a contract test rejects white below 45% on ink or ink below 58% on paper.

checks.name: dependency-script-policy
checks.evidence: pnpm allowBuilds explicitly rejects the unneeded unrs-resolver lifecycle script; pnpm reports no implicitly ignored builds and the frozen lock remains unchanged.

checks.name: cloud-ci
checks.evidence: Draft pull request 2 passed install, TypeScript, ESLint, 11/11 contracts, and CodeQL for Actions and JavaScript/TypeScript on commit c6e9e138; pinned Actions were modernized to their Node 24 releases.

checks.name: preview-build
checks.evidence: Vercel preview dpl_vfdhhbQntmK49yZPaTSas4SCVY2g built all 13 routes and reached READY on commit c6e9e13884b0c93de1a4ed11d3e0c84df9094ce3.

checks.name: preview-http
checks.evidence: The protected preview returned HTTP 200 on ten representative routes, exposed the conservative CSP and browser security headers, and had no runtime errors in the inspected one-hour window.

checks.name: export-inspection
checks.evidence: Desktop 1440x1000 and mobile 390x844 exports were inspected for the home, product, catalog, and studio surfaces. No horizontal overflow, clipping, lens collision, or content loss was observed.

checks.name: visual-qa
checks.evidence: The focus ring, catalog filter/search, three GSAP scroll beats, mobile static story, coarse-pointer route, reduced-motion route, responsive hierarchy, and browser console were inspected. Primary mobile navigation targets were raised to 44px.

score.notes: The exact product proof, editorial hierarchy, responsive layouts, all three scroll beats, reduced-motion behavior, mobile fallbacks, interaction targets, and clean production console pass. Fine-pointer parallax remains deliberately bounded and non-essential.

known_risks: The Vercel project has no public production deployment; the validated preview remains protected by team SSO.
The pull request remains draft until the final metadata and mobile-target patch receive exact-head CI and preview verification.
The in-app QA browser reports a coarse pointer, so fine-pointer parallax is source-reviewed and contract-tested rather than treated as essential product meaning.
No Tier B video may ship until provenance, poster, compression, crops, and exports are inspected.
